justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are explicitly covered: Consultation Service and Media Relay / SFU Container address R-01; Prescription & Interoperability Service addresses R-02; AI Inference Orchestrator handles R-03; and Consent Management Service with Cryptographic Consent Verifier Plugin satisfies R-04.
justifications.performance_efficiency: Bandwidth Adaptation & Congestion Controller enables degraded streaming under 300 kbit/s. Redis-backed rate limiting, Anycast frontend, BigQuery streaming writes, and Cloud Spanner ensure high-throughput, low-latency operational and analytical processing.
justifications.compatibility: FHIR & National Mapping Engine uses HAPI FHIR to support US HL7 FHIR and European national prescription formats. In addition, Regional API Gateways and Identity Providers integrate standard protocols including eIDAS, OAuth2/OIDC, and NCPDP.
justifications.usability: Patients and clinicians are served via Flutter Web / HTML5 / CSS UI (supporting WCAG 2.1 AA) and Native Mobile Apps. The Localization & Fault Transformation Component delivers localized error messages, and compliance officers have dedicated analytical access.
justifications.reliability: Regional TURN/STUN Relays adapt connections dynamically below 300 kbit/s to preserve audio calls. Prescription Outbox & Retry Processor uses Resilience4j circuit breakers and retries, while Regional Cloud Spanner ensures continuous transactional availability.
justifications.security: Regional Cloud Spanner and BigQuery datasets enforce regional data residency. Istio with SPIFFE/SPIRE delivers zero-trust mTLS, DTLS-SRTP secures media, Local State Encryption Manager uses AES-GCM, and Audit Logging Component guarantees MDR traceability.
justifications.maintainability: Containers exhibit clear separation of concerns (signaling, consent, interoperability, AI orchestration). Internal components like FHIR & National Mapping Engine and Consent Policy Engine isolate business rules, and ArgoCD enables declarative GitOps deployments.
justifications.portability: GKE Regional Clusters, Cloud Spanner, and Regional BigQuery datasets are explicitly provisioned across the specified GCP target regions (europe-west3 and us-central1). Native Mobile Apps and Web Applications use Flutter for cross-platform portability.

PERF-01.justification: GKE Regional Clusters, LiveKit Media Relay SFUs, and Managed Instance Groups running Coturn handle horizontal scaling for high-concurrency media sessions. The signaling controller efficiently decouples WebRTC negotiation from media forwarding.
sensitivity_points: SFU node autoscaling and CPU utilization during peak call connection spikes
STUN/TURN network throughput and port capacity on Compute Engine MIGs
tradeoffs: Media relay via SFU optimizes client bandwidth but increases server compute costs

PERF-02.justification: 50,000 requests per hour equates to under 15 requests per second. Python FastAPI on GKE easily handles this volume, using gRPC and asynchronous logging to BigQuery to maintain sub-3s latencies.
sensitivity_points: Upstream AI engine inference latency under peak concurrent loads
Synchronous Spanner write latency during inline inference logging
tradeoffs: Asynchronous BigQuery streaming improves latency but introduces minor analytical sync delay

AVAIL-01.justification: The architecture explicitly includes a Bandwidth Adaptation and Congestion Controller using WebRTC GCC/SVC to throttle video and prioritize audio below 300 kbit/s, while clinical notes persist via transactional Cloud Spanner storage.
sensitivity_points: Congestion control responsiveness when network drops sharply below 300 kbit/s
Audio codec priority enforcement over packet-loss-prone UDP connections
tradeoffs: Dropping video tracks preserves audio clarity but degrades consultation visual context

AVAIL-02.justification: The architecture provisions single-region deployments without defining a secondary US failover region or warm standby. If us-central1 fails entirely, restoring services within 1 hour without moving data to the EU cannot be guaranteed.
sensitivity_points: Absence of secondary US cloud region for disaster recovery and failover
Cloud Spanner configuration restricted to single-region instances
tradeoffs: Strict regional residency prevents active-passive replication to EU but risks regional downtime

MOD-01.justification: The Prescription & Interoperability Service isolates interoperability mechanisms inside the FHIR & National Mapping Engine and Pharmacy Integration Client, confining changes for new national standards strictly to that microservice adapter.
sensitivity_points: Extensibility of mapping abstractions when integrating non-FHIR national standards
Decoupling of core prescription models from region-specific clearinghouse protocols
tradeoffs: Using internal canonical models requires adapter translation overhead for national standards

MOD-02.justification: The AI Inference Orchestrator explicitly logs inputs, urgency outputs, and model versions to append-only Cloud Spanner audit tables and BigQuery datasets, enabling full auditability, rollback, and EU MDR compliance.
sensitivity_points: Immutable version tagging on all inference requests dispatched to external engines
Strict schema enforcement in BigQuery audit logs preventing model log corruption
tradeoffs: Logging full payload and model metadata increases storage overhead and write latency

SEC-01.justification: Cross-border requests are intercepted by Regional API Gateways and validated by the Cryptographic Consent Verifier Plugin and Consultation Workflow Manager against the Consent Management Service before accessing Regional Cloud Spanner.
sensitivity_points: Zero-trust mTLS verification between API gateways and cross-region services
Cryptographic integrity and expiration enforcement of patient consent tokens
tradeoffs: Strict consent validation on every request adds gRPC authorization overhead

SEC-02.justification: The Consent Management Service triggers immediate event-driven invalidation via Regional Pub/Sub and updates Regional Cloud Spanner. Row-level security and BigQuery dynamic data masking ensure research data access stops immediately and verifiably.
sensitivity_points: Pub/Sub message delivery latency for downstream cache and token invalidation
Audit trail immutability for proving revocation timestamps during regulatory audits
tradeoffs: Instant event-driven revocation requires distributed cache invalidation across services
